checked.claim: During the opening's veil the killer stays a participant of the room's LiveKit channel, so the victim's and a bystander's voice tile count them and 'Who you hear' names them with the portrait.
checked.why: placeVoices applies the Spectators', the eavesdrop's and the mask's rules over an account's row and no veil rule (grep 'veil' in voice.mjs: veiledIds, ownVeiled, micHold, moduleHoldsMic, settleTrialVoices only - all microphone). voiceClaim places the account by its token's room (locate()), so the killer is sent the crime room. channelCount counts every remote participant; paintList maps each to a user with participantUser (avclient-livekit's getParticipantFVTTUser, no token, flag or visibility read) and names it through voiceIdentity, which reads user.character / owned actor and nothing of a veil or mask (camera-view.mjs 205-240, no 'veil' or 'mask' in the file). mask-gm.mjs's own header names this channel as the reason the mask sends the killer to a silent room; the veil's header and e112v/DESIGN.md treat voice as the microphone alone. No test or recorded decision says the list may name a veiled killer. One limit on the scenario: an opening opened mid-day follows a token the victim may already have seen in the room before the open, so the strongest case is the Eclipse one (the declaration in the dark, the veil put on before the lights) and a bystander who enters after the open; that keeps it a rule broken in an ordinary situation of every direct murder in an Eclipse. The name needs avclient-livekit to map the participant (external, the reader's not_established); the count does not.

checked.claim: A masked killer's tile reads 'Disconnected' / 'You are not connected to voice.' and the mic line names only the microphone and only the reveal, so the killer does not learn they hear nobody or that the time of day ends it.
checked.why: The tile road is confirmed: maskedRow sends the silent room, applyBreakout leaves voice for it, voiceWord answers a special word only for external and the Eclipse's two holds, so a 'masked' hold on a disconnected Room falls to WORDS.disconnected with the offline sentence, and DRPG.Voice.held.masked says only the microphone and the reveal. But the failure scenario (the killer does not learn that she hears nobody, and reloads thinking voice broke) is contradicted by two other roads the reader did not cite: maskKiller whispers the killer DRPG.Mask.card at the mask's start, which says she can neither speak nor hear anyone until she reveals herself or the time of day ends and names the tile's Reveal button, and askReveal's window says the same (DRPG.Mask.ask). The tile itself keeps a Reveal yourself button while the mask stands. What is left is a tile word that disagrees with what the killer was told - text, not a wrong state in play.

checked.claim: A page that landed alone (landAloneFirst) and has no `desired` yet answers a drop by 'reconnecting' to its silent-room name, which landedCorrectly reads as landed once disconnected, so the drop card is dismissed with no connect, and the self-check repeats it every 45 s until the primary assigns a room.
checked.why: Traced whole: landAloneFirst writes client.breakoutRoom = silentRoomFor(userId) (drpg-eclipse-<id>), which silentFor matches for this user. onRoomDisconnected skips only for silentFor(desired), and desired is undefined, so voiceDropped(true) shows the card and schedules reconnect after RECONNECT_MS[0] = 1000 ms. reconnect with desired undefined calls applyBreakout(breakoutRoom, { remember: false }); landedCorrectly(silent room) returns roomState() === 'disconnected', true after a drop, so applyBreakout calls voiceBack() (the card goes) and returns 'unchanged' without game.webrtc.connect. selfCheck (SELF_CHECK_MS 45000) then finds !live(), shows the card and enqueues the same reconnect. No guard elsewhere keeps the silent name out of reconnect. The harm is narrow: the page was in a room of one before the drop, so what is wrong is the card (shown and taken down as if voice were back, again every 45 s) and that the reconnect does nothing, until the primary's answer, which is seconds normally and longer only while the account is `held` (voice.mjs 1095-1097). Wrong in a particular situation: minor holds.
